items.headline: With 93% of polling stations counted, Israel's Central Elections Committee put Netanyahu's bloc at 53 seats, Eisenkot's bloc at 48 and the Arab parties at 19
items.summary: Likud held 26 seats and Yashar! 21 in the near-final tally, leaving the Netanyahu bloc eight short of the 61 needed; more than 500,000 double-envelope ballots from soldiers and voters outside their assigned stations were still to be counted. The committee has not certified the result and publishes official figures on 4 November, after which the president has seven days to hand a candidate the mandate.
items.why: Neither bloc can govern without the Arab lists or defectors, so plan on a caretaker government in Israel, and on the Iran question staying open, for weeks rather than days.

items.headline: GitHub made Copilot Fusion generally available and let Enterprise customers use every Copilot feature without a subscription, paying only for the AI credits they consume
items.summary: Fusion replaces picking a model with picking an effort level (Standard, High or Max) and routes each prompt across models, billed at each model's standard rate with a 30% discount on paid plans for a limited time; GitHub said Fusion Max scored 60 on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index, within two points of Claude Code with Opus 5.5 Max, at about half the API cost and 40% less time per task. The credit-only Enterprise arrangement is available through GitHub Sales now with self-serve to follow, existing Business and Enterprise plans continue, and Universe also shipped Copilot Projects for parallel multi-repo agent sessions and a code review Max tier.
items.why: If your team pays for Copilot, benchmark Fusion against your pinned model while the 30% discount runs, and reprice seats against a credit budget before the next renewal.

items.headline: GitHub's Octoverse report said agents started over 40% of pull requests in September, up from 17% in March, about 110 million in the month
items.summary: The report counted more than 225 million developers, 34.3 billion commits and 1.3 billion merged pull requests in the trailing twelve months, with TypeScript ahead of Python as the language with the most contributors. 55% of monthly Copilot users now use agentic features, up from 35% a year earlier, and paying users drew on 47 distinct models in September with none above 25% of requests.
items.why: Agent-drafted pull requests are now the main path into GitHub repositories, so size code review, CI minutes and merge policy for that volume rather than for hand-typed diffs.

items.headline: Google DeepMind announced Gemini 4 Carbon, first on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at 59, and restricted it to cyber defenders through its Fairwind Program
items.summary: Google quoted 88.2% on SEC-bench Pro for finding vulnerabilities and 54.8% on ExploitGym for exploiting them, said it is taking part in the US government's voluntary pre-release testing, and gave no date for developer or consumer access. Introductory pricing matches Gemini 4 Argon at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, rising to $4 and $20 after the introductory period.
items.why: Do not plan a Carbon migration yet, and note that Google has now priced its next tier at double Argon once the introductory period ends.

items.headline: Node.js 26 entered Long Term Support as 26.13.0 'Lithium', with updates through April 2029
items.summary: The release changes only release metadata to mark LTS status; Node.js 24 moved to Maintenance on 20 October. Official Linux binaries have linked against libatomic since Node 25, so some distributions need it installed when moving a 22 or 24 deployment to 26.
items.why: Move production services and CI base images from Node 24 to 26 now, and check libatomic on minimal Linux images before you do.

items.headline: The Fed held at 3.75–4.00% on a 10–2 vote, with Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack dissenting in favour of a quarter-point hike
items.summary: The statement said economic activity is expanding at a strong pace, inflation remains elevated and the Committee will gather more information before deciding the stance needed for a timely return to 2%, adding that it 'will deliver price stability'. It was the first meeting since September's hike, the Fed's first increase since July 2023.
items.why: Two dissents for a hike and no easing language make a December increase the base case, so price floating-rate debt and cash yields on 4%-plus policy into 2027.

items.headline: The Bank of Canada raised its policy rate 25 basis points to 2.5%, its first increase since July 2023, and said a further rise could be needed
items.summary: The Bank cited oil prices that remain persistently high in the eighth month of the Middle East conflict, CPI inflation around 3% since April and expected to reach about 3.5% by year-end, and growth tracking about 2% in the third quarter. The next decision is on 9 December.
items.why: Canada has joined the Fed and the ECB in tightening against energy-driven inflation, so treat the 2026 rate cycle across the G7 as upward until oil breaks.

items.headline: John Healey's first Budget raised tax on UK savings and property income by a further two points from April 2027 and doubled the bank surcharge to 6% for 15 months
items.summary: Savings and property income will be taxed at 24%, 44% and 49% from April 2027, on top of last year's two-point rise, while the £20,000 cash ISA limit stays and employment and dividend income are untouched; the bank surcharge rise raises £1.5 billion and ends 31 March 2028. The Treasury put headroom against the stability rule at £15 billion in 2029-30, £9 billion less than in March, funded a £100 household energy payment in 2027 and extended the electricity VAT cut to July 2027.
items.why: UK bank earnings carry a 6% surcharge for the next 15 months and unwrapped UK savings income loses another two points, so ISA-wrapped holdings and non-bank exposure are the better UK positions from April.

items.headline: Keystone said attackers stole the key its hardware wallets use to prove they are genuine, paused shipments and will destroy 18,835 unsold devices
items.summary: The 20 October breach of its website through a third-party monitoring tool also exposed 25,964 buyer records, some kept past the company's 180-day deletion promise. Keystone said the key cannot be changed in shipped devices, that recovery phrases and private keys were not involved, that devices delivered before 20 October which pass its check are genuine, and that any call, text or letter offering a recall, refund or help moving funds is a scam.
items.why: If you hold a Keystone, treat any device received after 20 October as unverified until support confirms it, and expect targeted phishing against the leaked address list.
